title: NYC Sightseeing Guide License Exam
page_numbering: PDF page index (1 = first page of the PDF file); null for HTML pages

questions.question: According to DCWP's Study Reference, which borough do the Sightseeing Guide exam questions predominantly focus on?
questions.explanation: The exam focuses on general NYC knowledge, predominantly Manhattan, but includes questions about all five boroughs.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide Study Reference (PDF)
source.quote: focus on overall general New York City knowledge—predominantly Manhattan—but the test will include questions about all five boroughs.

questions.question: Which of these authors is on the Study Reference's list of New York writers that the exam may ask about?
questions.explanation: The literature list is limited to E. B. White, Langston Hughes, Edith Wharton, Washington Irving, Paule Marshall, Jack Finney, Walt Whitman, O. Henry and F. Scott Fitzgerald.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide Study Reference (PDF)
source.quote: E. B. White, Langston Hughes, Edith Wharton, Washington Irving, Paule Marshall, Jack Finney, Walt Whitman, O. Henry

questions.question: Which author on this list is NOT one of the nine writers named in the Study Reference's literature topic?
questions.explanation: Melville is not on the list. The nine are White, Hughes, Wharton, Irving, Marshall, Finney, Whitman, O. Henry and Fitzgerald.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide Study Reference (PDF)
source.quote: the list will be limited to the following: E. B. White, Langston Hughes, Edith Wharton, Washington Irving, Paule Marshall

questions.question: Which two garden cemeteries does the Study Reference specifically name under 'Parks and Parkways'?
questions.explanation: Topic 12 covers parks and parkways plus Greenwood and Woodlawn Cemeteries.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide Study Reference (PDF)
source.quote: Parks and Parkways, plus Greenwood and Woodlawn Cemeteries

questions.question: Which 'Walk of Fame' does the Study Reference associate with Brooklyn Botanic Garden?
questions.explanation: The Study Reference lists the Brooklyn Botanic Garden's 'Celebrity Walk' among the walks of fame.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide Study Reference (PDF)
source.quote: Brooklyn Botanic Garden’s “Celebrity Walk,”

questions.question: Where is the 'Fashion Walk' that the Study Reference lists among the city's walks of fame?
questions.explanation: The Study Reference names Seventh Avenue's 'Fashion Walk'.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide Study Reference (PDF)
source.quote: “Walks of Fame” include Seventh Avenue’s “Fashion Walk,”

questions.question: Which walk of fame does the Study Reference associate with the Second Avenue Deli?
questions.explanation: The Second Avenue Deli's 'Yiddish Theatre Walk' is listed.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide Study Reference (PDF)
source.quote: Second Avenue Deli’s “Yiddish Theatre Walk,”

questions.question: Which practicum topic does the Study Reference flag as 'very important'?
options: Legal routings and pick-up/drop-off locations for tour buses
questions.explanation: Topic 16 (legal tour bus routings, pick-up/drop-off locations and the Midtown Thru Streets program) is marked 'This is very important!'

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide Study Reference (PDF)
source.quote: Legal routings and passenger pick-up/drop-off locations for tour buses; the Midtown Thru Streets Program. This is very important!

questions.question: Which agency's bus regulations does the Study Reference say guides are legally obligated to follow when directing bus drivers?
questions.explanation: Guides must strictly adhere to NYC DOT bus regulations when directing bus drivers.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide Study Reference (PDF)
source.quote: Please pay special attention to the New York City Department of Transportation (DOT) bus regulations.

questions.question: Under which topic does the Study Reference include the Arts for Transit program?
questions.explanation: Topic 1, 'Getting There', points to mta.info for general information and the Arts for Transit program.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide Study Reference (PDF)
source.quote: check mta.info for general information, and for information about the Arts for Transit Program.

questions.question: Which planning concept does the Study Reference's architecture topic say candidates should comprehend?
questions.explanation: Topic 11 asks for comprehension of the 'grid plan' and its impacts.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide Study Reference (PDF)
source.quote: Comprehension of “grid plan” and its impacts.

questions.question: The history topic in the Study Reference runs from which group to the present day?
questions.explanation: Topic 3 covers rudimentary history 'from the Algonquin Indians to the present day'.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide Study Reference (PDF)
source.quote: New York City History – Rudimentary history from the Algonquin Indians to the present day

questions.question: What does the Study Reference say about failing the exam on your first attempt?
options: You must pay the license fee again
You must take a classroom course
You must wait one year to retest
There is no penalty for failing on the first attempt
questions.explanation: There is no penalty for a first-attempt fail. After two fails, the exam fee must be paid again.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide Study Reference (PDF)
source.quote: There is no penalty for failing the Professional Licensing Examination for New York City Sightseeing Guides on your first attempt.

questions.question: Which organization's website does the Study Reference cite for an excellent range of tours?
options: The Guides Association of New York City (GANYC)
questions.explanation: The Study Reference points to GANYC's website for a range of tours.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide Study Reference (PDF)
source.quote: An excellent range of tours is listed on the Web site for the Guides Association of New York City

questions.question: How old must a Sightseeing Guide licence applicant be?
questions.explanation: DCWP requires Sightseeing Guide applicants to be at least 18 years old.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide License Application Checklist
source.quote: Sightseeing Guide applicants must be at least 18 years old.

questions.question: How many questions are on the Sightseeing Guide exam?
questions.explanation: The exam has 150 questions.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide License Application Checklist
source.quote: The exam consists of 150 questions.

questions.question: How many correct answers are needed to pass the Sightseeing Guide exam?
questions.explanation: You must answer at least 97 of the 150 questions correctly.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide License Application Checklist
source.quote: You must answer a minimum of 97 questions correctly to pass.

questions.question: What is the Sightseeing Guide exam fee?
options: $50, nonrefundable and separate from the license fee
questions.explanation: The $50 exam fee is separate from the license fee and is nonrefundable.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide License Application Checklist
source.quote: The $50 exam fee is separate from the license fee and is nonrefundable.

questions.question: After DCWP's exam vendor has your information, how long do you have to take and pass the exam?
questions.explanation: You have 60 days from when your information appears in ExamBuilder's system.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide License Application Checklist
source.quote: You have 60 days to take and pass the exam from the time your information appears in ExamBuilder’s system.

questions.question: What is the license period for a Sightseeing Guide license?
questions.explanation: The license period is 2 years, expiring March 31 in even years.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide License Application Checklist
source.quote: License Period: 2 years Expiration Date: March 31 in Even Years

questions.question: Sightseeing Guide licenses expire on which date?
questions.explanation: Guide licenses expire March 31 in even years.

source.title: DCWP Sightseeing Guide License Application Checklist
source.quote: Expiration Date: March 31 in Even Years

questions.question: If you fail the Sightseeing Guide exam twice, what must you do to retake it?
options: Reapply for a new license and be fingerprinted
questions.explanation: After a second failure, guide applicants must pay the $50 exam fee again.

source.title: DCWP Licensing FAQs: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: You must pay the $50 exam fee again in order to retake the exam.

questions.question: After a first failed attempt, how long must you wait before scheduling a second attempt (per DCWP's exam FAQ)?
questions.explanation: The FAQ says to wait 24 hours from the failed attempt before scheduling the second attempt.

source.title: DCWP Licensing FAQs: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: You must wait 24 hours from your failed attempt before scheduling the exam for a second attempt.

questions.question: What happens if you miss a scheduled exam without rescheduling in advance?
options: You get a free make-up exam
questions.explanation: Missing a scheduled exam without rescheduling counts as an automatic fail.

source.title: DCWP Licensing FAQs: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: If you miss a scheduled exam without rescheduling in advance, you will automatically fail

questions.question: By when must you request a new exam date if you need to reschedule?
options: 5:00 p.m. the day before the original exam date
questions.explanation: Requests must be made by 5:00 p.m. the day before the originally scheduled exam.

source.title: DCWP Licensing FAQs: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: you must request a new exam date by 5:00 p.m. the day before the originally scheduled exam date

questions.question: Who administers DCWP's licensing exams, including the Sightseeing Guide exam?
questions.explanation: ExamBuilder administers all DCWP licensing exams.

source.title: DCWP Licensing FAQs: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: ExamBuilder administers all DCWP licensing exams.

questions.question: Which applicants must take the Sightseeing Guide exam?
questions.explanation: The Sightseeing Guide exam is required of new applicants only.

source.title: DCWP Licensing FAQs: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: Sightseeing Guide (NEW applicants only)

questions.question: Under DCWP's definition, a sightseeing bus carries at least how many passengers?
questions.explanation: A sightseeing bus operates for hire taking eight or more passengers to places of interest from a point in NYC.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Sightseeing Bus (PDF)
source.quote: A sightseeing bus is a bus that operates for hire either to take eight or more passengers from a fixed point in New York City

questions.question: On a DCWP-licensed sightseeing bus, what must the departure-time signs say?
options: "This bus leaves (time) sharp or money refunded upon request."
questions.explanation: Every sightseeing bus must have two departure signs with this wording, removed once the bus departs.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Sightseeing Bus (PDF)
source.quote: “This bus leaves (specifying time) sharp or money refunded upon request.”

questions.question: What is an 'open-air sightseeing bus' under DCWP's checklist?
options: A bus that only tours parks
A sightseeing bus with seating that is partially or entirely unenclosed
questions.explanation: DCWP defines it by partially or entirely unenclosed seating.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Sightseeing Bus (PDF)
source.quote: An open-air sightseeing bus is a sightseeing bus that has seating that is partially or entirely unenclosed.

questions.question: Under the NYC Traffic Rules, what must a tour or charter bus operator carry at all times?
options: A list of passengers' home addresses
A printed copy of the subway map
A route slip listing origin, destination and streets in between
A DCWP guide license for each passenger
questions.explanation: Bus operators must prepare a detailed route slip in advance and keep it in their possession.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: The route slip must include the points of origin and destination of the trip and the streets that they plan to take in between.

questions.question: Which streets must tour bus drivers generally travel on in NYC?
options: Any street with two or more lanes
Designated truck routes, except when needed to reach a destination
questions.explanation: Bus drivers must use truck routes, leaving them only to reach destinations.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: Bus drivers must travel along New York City truck routes except when local bus routes or other roads are needed to reach their destinations.

questions.question: When a bus leaves a truck route to reach a destination, where must it leave the route?
options: Only at a bridge or tunnel
At the nearest intersection to the destination
questions.explanation: Drivers leave truck routes at the nearest intersection to the destination and return at the nearest possible location.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: Drivers must leave the truck routes at the nearest intersection to their destination and return at the nearest possible location.

questions.question: What does a bus need to use parkways or the FDR Drive?
options: Nothing; buses may always use parkways
questions.explanation: Buses may not use parkways or the FDR Drive without a Highway Travel Permit.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: Buses are not permitted to use parkways or FDR Drive without a Highway Travel Permit.

questions.question: What is the per-trip fee charter buses must pay in NYC, per NYC DOT?
questions.explanation: Charter buses pay $1.50 per trip; stickers come in books of ten for $15.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: Charter Buses must pay fee of $1.50 per trip.

questions.question: What is the general bus parking meter rate in Manhattan?
questions.explanation: The general meter rate for buses is $20 per hour.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: The general meter rate for buses is $20 per hour, payable at parking meters

questions.question: What is the time limit at bus parking meters?
questions.explanation: Bus meters have a three-hour time limit.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: Meters have a three-hour time limit

questions.question: When are bus parking meters in effect?
options: Daily 7 am to 7 pm, except Sundays
questions.explanation: Bus meters run daily 7 am to 7 pm, except Sundays.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: Bus parking meters are in effect daily from 7 am to 7 pm, except Sundays

questions.question: At passenger drop-off zones, when is bus idling strictly prohibited?
questions.explanation: Idling is strictly prohibited above 40°F, and allowed up to three minutes at 40°F or below.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: Idling is strictly prohibited when the temperature is above 40 degrees (Fahrenheit)

questions.question: Can a bus park in a passenger drop-off and pick-up zone?
options: Yes, if the driver stays aboard
Yes, for up to one hour
No, these zones are for expeditious drop-off and pick-up only
questions.explanation: Buses may not park in drop-off/pick-up zones for any amount of time.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: Buses may not park in these zones for any amount of time

questions.question: Where may a bus operator NOT pick up or drop off passengers?
options: At the curb in a legal loading area
In a vehicle travel lane or a 'No Stopping Anytime' zone
questions.explanation: Pick-ups and drop-offs are banned in travel lanes and No Stopping Anytime zones.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: Bus operators may not pick up or drop off passengers in a vehicle travel lane or in any zone where "No Stopping Anytime" is posted

questions.question: What must a bus operator do while passengers are loading or unloading?
options: Turn on hazard lights and leave
Escort the group to the attraction
questions.explanation: Operators must stay with their vehicle during loading and unloading.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: Bus operators must stay with their vehicle while passengers are loading or unloading

questions.question: Is double-parking a bus ever permitted in Manhattan?
questions.explanation: Double-parking is not permitted at any time.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: Double-parking is not permitted at any time

questions.question: How long can buses park in Lower Manhattan?
questions.explanation: Buses cannot park in Lower Manhattan for more than three hours; operators may use private off-street lots.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: Buses cannot park in Lower Manhattan for more than three hours.

questions.question: Bus parking near the World Trade Center is available only to which buses?
options: Buses with permits transporting groups registered with the 9/11 Memorial & Museum
Any bus that pays the meter
questions.explanation: For security reasons, WTC-area bus parking is permit-only for registered 9/11 Memorial & Museum groups.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: bus parking located near the World Trade Center is available only to buses with permits that are transporting groups registered to visit

questions.question: How does NYC DOT encourage tour groups to visit the 9/11 Memorial & Museum?
options: By charter bus parked on Church Street
By mass transit instead of charter buses
questions.explanation: DOT strongly encourages mass transit because bus parking is very limited.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: NYC DOT strongly encourages tour groups planning trips to the 9/11 Memorial & Museum use mass transit instead of charter buses.

questions.question: Where can tour buses coming from New Jersey park all day for a fee and use ferry or PATH service to Lower Manhattan?
questions.explanation: Buses can park at Liberty State Park (NJ Turnpike Exit 14B) and take a ferry or PATH.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: Tour buses coming from New Jersey can park all day at Liberty State Park for a fee

questions.question: Which agencies strictly enforce NYC's tour and charter bus rules, per NYC DOT?
options: NYPD and the Department of Environmental Protection
questions.explanation: The rules are subject to strict enforcement by NYPD and DEP.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: subject to strict enforcement by the New York City Police Department and the New York City Department of Environmental Protection.

questions.question: In NYC DOT's holiday-season motor coach rules, which East River crossing is NOT permitted for buses?
questions.explanation: Permitted river crossings are all crossings except the Brooklyn Bridge.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: Permitted River Crossings All river crossings except Brooklyn Bridge

questions.question: In NYC DOT's holiday-season motor coach rules, where are bus pick-ups and drop-offs prohibited?
questions.explanation: Fifth Avenue between 32nd and 59th Streets is a prohibited pick-up and drop-off area in the holiday rules.

source.title: NYC DOT: Charter & Tour Buses
source.quote: Prohibited Pick-Up & Drop-Off Areas Fifth Avenue between 32nd and 59th Streets

questions.question: What document must truck drivers have on hand showing origin and destination, per DOT truck routing rules?
options: A bill of lading or similar document
A route map signed by NYPD
questions.explanation: Truck drivers must carry a bill of lading or similar document. Bus operators carry a route slip for the same purpose.

source.title: NYC DOT: Truck Routing
source.quote: Truck drivers must always have on hand a bill of lading, or similar document, showing the points of origin and destination of the trip.

questions.question: Which truck route network must be used by trucks with neither an origin nor a destination within the borough?
questions.explanation: Through routes are for trips passing through a borough; local routes are for trips that start or end in it.

source.title: NYC DOT: Truck Routing
source.quote: must be used by trucks that have neither an origin or destination within the borough.

questions.question: How long has the City operated the Staten Island Ferry?
questions.explanation: The City has run the ferry since 1905.

source.title: NYC DOT: Staten Island Ferry Facts
source.quote: The City has operated the Staten Island Ferry since 1905.

questions.question: How long is the Staten Island Ferry run between St. George and Whitehall?
questions.explanation: The ferry makes a 5.2-mile run between St. George Terminal and Whitehall Terminal.

source.title: NYC DOT: Staten Island Ferry Facts
source.quote: 5.2-mile run between the St. George Terminal in Staten Island and the Whitehall Terminal in Lower Manhattan.

questions.question: What is the Manhattan terminal of the Staten Island Ferry called?
questions.explanation: The Manhattan end is Whitehall Terminal; the Staten Island end is St. George.

source.title: NYC DOT: Staten Island Ferry Facts
source.quote: between the St. George Terminal in Staten Island and the Whitehall Terminal in Lower Manhattan.

questions.question: When does the Staten Island Ferry run?
options: 24 hours a day, 365 days a year
questions.explanation: The ferry runs around the clock all year.

source.title: NYC DOT: Staten Island Ferry Facts
source.quote: The Ferry runs 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

questions.question: How much does it cost to ride the Staten Island Ferry?
questions.explanation: NYC DOT provides free service between Staten Island and Lower Manhattan.

source.title: NYC DOT: Staten Island Ferry
source.quote: providing free service between Staten Island and Lower Manhattan every day of the week, year-round.

questions.question: Roughly how many passengers does the Staten Island Ferry carry each year?
questions.explanation: The ferry carries over 16 million passengers annually.

source.title: NYC DOT: Staten Island Ferry Facts
source.quote: The Ferry carries over 16 million passengers annually

questions.question: During rush hours, how often does the Staten Island Ferry depart?
questions.explanation: Rush hours use a four-boat schedule with 15 minutes between departures.

source.title: NYC DOT: Staten Island Ferry Facts
source.quote: During rush hours, the ferry runs on a four-boat schedule, with 15 minutes between departures.

questions.question: Which Staten Island Ferry boat is the first named to honor the history of Black New Yorkers on Staten Island?
questions.explanation: Sandy Ground honors a free Black community dating back to 1828.

source.title: NYC DOT: Staten Island Ferry Facts
source.quote: Sandy Ground is the first Staten Island Ferry boat named to honor the rich history of Black New Yorkers living on Staten Island.

questions.question: Dorothy Day, namesake of a Staten Island ferry, led which movement?
questions.explanation: Dorothy Day was a convert to Catholicism who led the Catholic Worker movement.

source.title: NYC DOT: Staten Island Ferry Facts
source.quote: Day was a convert to Catholicism who led the Catholic Worker movement.

questions.question: Which is the largest-capacity Staten Island ferry, carrying 5,200 passengers?
questions.explanation: The Barberi Class Samuel I. Newhouse carries 5,200 passengers.

source.title: NYC DOT: Staten Island Ferry Facts
source.quote: The Newhouse entered service in 1982. The boat carries 5,200 passengers

questions.question: Who designed the Brooklyn Bridge?
questions.explanation: John A. Roebling designed it; construction ran 1869-1883.

source.title: NYC DOT: Brooklyn Bridge
source.quote: The Brooklyn Bridge was designed by John A. Roebling.

questions.question: When was the Brooklyn Bridge completed?
questions.explanation: Construction began in 1869 and was completed in 1883.

source.title: NYC DOT: Brooklyn Bridge
source.quote: Construction began in 1869 and was completed in 1883.

questions.question: At its completion, the Brooklyn Bridge held what record?
options: Longest suspension bridge in the world
questions.explanation: It was the world's longest suspension bridge at the time.

source.title: NYC DOT: Brooklyn Bridge
source.quote: At the time, it was the longest suspension bridge in the world.

questions.question: Which two neighborhoods does the Brooklyn Bridge connect?
options: The Lower East Side and Williamsburg
questions.explanation: The Brooklyn Bridge connects Lower Manhattan and Brooklyn Heights.

source.title: NYC DOT: Brooklyn Bridge
source.quote: The iconic Brooklyn Bridge connects Lower Manhattan and Brooklyn Heights.

questions.question: When was the Brooklyn Bridge designated a National Historic Landmark?
questions.explanation: National Historic Landmark in 1964; National Historic Civil Engineering Landmark in 1972; NYC Landmark in 1967.

source.title: NYC DOT: Brooklyn Bridge
source.quote: The Brooklyn Bridge was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1964

questions.question: What opened on the Brooklyn Bridge in September 2021?
questions.explanation: A two-way protected bike lane opened, replacing one vehicle lane.

source.title: NYC DOT: Brooklyn Bridge
source.quote: In September 2021, a two-way protected bike lane opened along the Brooklyn Bridge

questions.question: Which neighborhoods does the Manhattan Bridge connect?
questions.explanation: The Manhattan Bridge connects Chinatown and Downtown Brooklyn.

source.title: NYC DOT: Manhattan Bridge
source.quote: The Manhattan Bridge connects Chinatown in Lower Manhattan and Downtown Brooklyn.

questions.question: Which is the youngest of NYC DOT's three East River suspension bridges, completed in 1909?
questions.explanation: The Manhattan Bridge (1909) is the youngest of the three suspension bridges.

source.title: NYC DOT: Manhattan Bridge
source.quote: The Manhattan Bridge was completed in 1909 and it is the youngest of the three NYC DOT East River suspension bridges.

questions.question: Which architectural firm designed the Manhattan Bridge's stone portal and plaza (and also the main New York Public Library)?
questions.explanation: Carrère and Hastings designed the portal and plaza.

source.title: NYC DOT: Manhattan Bridge
source.quote: designed by the architectural team of Carrère and Hastings, which also designed the main branch of the New York Public Library.

questions.question: The Manhattan Bridge was the first bridge built using which engineering theory?
questions.explanation: It was the first built on deflection theory, so it lacks massive stiffening trusses.

source.title: NYC DOT: Manhattan Bridge
source.quote: The bridge was the first to be built based on deflection theory

questions.question: What type of bridge is the Ed Koch Queensboro (59th Street) Bridge?
questions.explanation: It is the only one of the four great East River bridges that is not a suspension bridge.

source.title: NYC DOT: Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge
source.quote: is the only one of the four great East River Bridges that is not a suspension bridge.

questions.question: The Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge is also known as what?
questions.explanation: It is also known as the 59th Street Bridge.

source.title: NYC DOT: Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge
source.quote: The Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge, also known as the 59th Street Bridge, is a cantilever truss bridge over the East River.

questions.question: Which island provides footing for the piers of the Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge?
questions.explanation: The bridge passes over Roosevelt Island, which supports its piers.

source.title: NYC DOT: Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge
source.quote: The bridge is conveniently located over Roosevelt Island, which provides the perfect footing for the piers.

questions.question: Which bridge engineer designed the Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge?
questions.explanation: Gustav Lindenthal designed it with architect Henry Hornbostel (spelled Hornbosted on DOT's page).

source.title: NYC DOT: Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge
source.quote: Designed by the bridge engineer Gustav Lindenthal

questions.question: When it opened in 1903, the Williamsburg Bridge held what record?
options: Longest suspension bridge in the world
questions.explanation: In 1903 it was the longest suspension bridge in the world.

source.title: NYC DOT: Williamsburg Bridge
source.quote: When it opened in 1903, the Williamsburg Bridge was the longest suspension bridge in the world

questions.question: Which subway lines cross the Williamsburg Bridge?
questions.explanation: Two transit tracks carrying the J, M and Z run between the roadways.

source.title: NYC DOT: Williamsburg Bridge
source.quote: with two rapid transit tracks (J, M, and Z subway lines) sandwiched in between.

questions.question: What was New York City's first bridge?
options: The King's Bridge (1693) over Spuyten Duyvil Creek
questions.explanation: The King's Bridge, built 1693, spanned Spuyten Duyvil Creek between Manhattan and the Bronx.

source.title: NYC DOT: Bridges
source.quote: New York City's first bridge, known as the King's Bridge, was constructed in 1693.

questions.question: Which is the oldest NYC bridge still open to passengers or vehicles?
questions.explanation: The Brooklyn Bridge, opened 1883, is the oldest still open.

source.title: NYC DOT: Bridges
source.quote: The oldest bridge that is open to passengers or vehicles is the Brooklyn Bridge, which opened in 1883.

questions.question: Do drivers pay tolls on bridges operated by NYC DOT?
options: No, there are no tolls on NYC DOT bridges
Only the Brooklyn Bridge is tolled
questions.explanation: There are no tolls on NYC DOT-operated bridges.

source.title: NYC DOT: Bridges
source.quote: There are no tolls on bridges operated by NYC DOT.

questions.question: Which landmarked bridge is operated by NYC Parks rather than NYC DOT?
questions.explanation: The three landmarked bridges not run by DOT are the George Washington Bridge (Port Authority), the High Bridge (Parks) and Hell Gate Bridge (Amtrak).

source.title: NYC DOT: Bridges
source.quote: the George Washington Bridge (Port Authority), the High Bridge ( NYC Department of Parks & Recreation ), and Hell Gate Bridge (Amtrak).

questions.question: What is Wards Island's former name, per NYC DOT?
questions.explanation: Wards Island was formerly called Great Barn Island.

source.title: NYC DOT: Harlem River Bridges
source.quote: The first known bridge to Wards Island (formerly Great Barn Island) was built in 1807

questions.question: Who built Gracie Mansion, and in what year?
questions.explanation: Shipping merchant Archibald Gracie built the wood-frame country house in 1799.

source.title: Gracie Mansion: A Student Guide to the People's House (PDF)
source.quote: In 1799, Gracie built a wood-frame house on the land.

questions.question: What was Archibald Gracie's profession?
questions.explanation: Gracie was a successful Scottish-born shipping merchant.

source.title: Gracie Mansion: A Student Guide to the People's House (PDF)
source.quote: Archibald Gracie, a successful Scottish-born shipping merchant.

questions.question: Who was the first mayor to live at Gracie Mansion?
questions.explanation: La Guardia moved in with his family in 1942.

source.title: Gracie Mansion: A Student Guide to the People's House (PDF)
source.quote: Mayor Fiorello H. La Guardia moved into the house with his family and was the first mayor to live at Gracie Mansion.

questions.question: In what year did Gracie Mansion become the official residence of the Mayor?
questions.explanation: Gracie Mansion became the official mayoral residence in 1942.

source.title: Gracie Mansion: A Student Guide to the People's House (PDF)
source.quote: In 1942, Gracie Mansion became the official residence of the Mayor of the City of New York.

questions.question: What 'first' did New York achieve when Gracie Mansion became the mayor's home?
options: First city with a female mayor
First city with a public park
First U.S. city with an official mayoral residence
questions.explanation: New York became the first U.S. city with a special home for its mayor.

source.title: Gracie Mansion Conservancy brochure (PDF)
source.quote: making New York the first city in the United States with an official mayoral residence.

questions.question: Which museum had its first home at Gracie Mansion, starting in 1923?
options: Museum of the City of New York
questions.explanation: The Museum of the City of New York began at Gracie Mansion in 1923 and moved to Fifth Avenue in 1932.

source.title: Gracie Mansion: A Student Guide to the People's House (PDF)
